newsitem.title: UK: Syria cuts Mar Light crude 23 cts, some traders moan.
newsitem.headline: Syria cuts Mar Light crude 23 cts, some traders moan.

text.p: Syria's state oil company Sytrol has agreed a 23-cent cut in the price of its Light crude oil for March in the face of stiff opposition from some southern European customers who wanted a bigger discount, traders said.
Key lifters in northwest Europe had accepted Sytrol's final offer of Dated Brent less 50 cents a barrel for Syrian Light, down from Dated Brent less 27 cents in February.
"I'm afraid if two or three of the big lifters agree then the rest have to follow," said a Mediterranean refiner.
"That will probably turn out to be the final price," said a trader at a major oil company.

Some customers, including French and Spanish refiners, were said to be considering returning March cargoes. Traders said their resistance was understandable, given poor refining margins, but was likely to crumble.

"Even at (Dated) minus 50 cents, Syrian Light is still not competitive given the ample supplies of sour crude but if they return cargoes they will lose those volumes next year when contracts are renegotiated," said one.

Traders said less sophisticated refineries have to treat Syrian Light as a sour crude, placing it in direct competition with grades like Russian Urals and Iraqi Kirkuk -- both currently well supplied in the Mediterranean -- while other lifters are able to apply sweet crude economics to the grade.
Late last month, Sytrol agreed a five-cent cut in the price of its heavy Souedie crude, pegging it at Dated Brent -$4.80 a barrel in March.
Traders said the modest Souedie cut reflected a seasonal improvement in margins for the crude, which has a heavy bitumen yield.
